description: Exploit the empirical observation that higher-order epistasis in proteins is sparse — most fitness effects are well-approximated by first and second-order terms. Build a sparse interaction graph from cheap pairwise evaluations, then search only the connected components and high-interaction subsets, pruning the combinatorial space by orders of magnitude.
mathematical_formalization: Model fitness f(x) = sum_i alpha_i * x_i + sum_{i<j} beta_{ij} * x_i * x_j + epsilon, where x_i encodes amino acid at position i. Estimate beta_{ij} from O(k^2 * 19) pairwise evaluations. Define interaction graph G where edge (i,j) exists iff |beta_{ij}| > threshold. Decompose search into connected components of G.
analogical_connections: Compressed sensing: sparse signals recovered from few measurements — epistatic interactions are the sparse signal
Ising models in statistical physics: pairwise interaction terms define phase behavior
Ranganathan (2019) showed epistasis up to 13th order is extraordinarily sparse
implementation_hypothesis: Phase 1: Score all single mutants. Phase 2: Score pairwise double mutants for candidate pairs. Phase 3: Build interaction graph, threshold edges. Phase 4: Exhaustive or beam search within connected components. Phase 5: Combine per-component solutions.
experiment_seed: Use Mega-scale double mutant data to validate sparsity: compute pairwise epistasis for 50 proteins, measure fraction of pairs with |epistasis| > 0.5 kcal/mol.
